title: Deployment Rollback Grouping SOP — Full Procedure
content:
Deployment Rollback Grouping SOP (Version 1)

Rule ID: f07_deployment_rollback_grouping_v1

PURPOSE
This SOP defines the procedure for triaging child failure tickets caused by a specific deployment event. Deployment events are identified by a unique release_hash value.

PROCEDURE:

1. IDENTIFY CHILD TICKETS
   - Look for the root deployment ticket (ticket_type: deploy-event) only to determine the release_hash.
   - Identify all child failure tickets that explicitly reference the same release_hash in their description.
   - A child ticket is one where the release_hash in the description matches the root deployment event's release_hash.
   - Do NOT match tickets by service name alone — only by release_hash.
   - Do NOT include tickets referencing a different release_hash, even if they are for the same service.

2. UPDATE CHILD TICKETS ONLY
   - For each confirmed child ticket (matching release_hash):
     - Set priority = high
     - Set category = incident
     - Set tags = [deploy-child, root-event-pending]
   - DO NOT update the root deployment ticket. It is context for grouping, not a child failure ticket.
   - DO NOT close any child ticket — leave status as open for on-call engineer review.
   - DO NOT resolve or mark as fixed — the root cause is still pending rollback decision.

3. EXCLUSIONS
   - Do NOT update the root deployment event ticket.
   - Do NOT update tickets from unrelated deployments (different release_hash), even if they mention 'rollback' in the title or description.
   - Do NOT update service-level tickets that have no release_hash or reference a different hash.
   - Matching by service name alone is INSUFFICIENT — always require release_hash match.

4. PHRASING VARIATIONS
   - Child tickets may describe the hash in different ways: 'related to vwx234 deployment', 'vwx234 rollout issue', 'caused by hash vwx234', etc.
   - The release_hash value itself must be present and must match the root event's hash.

IMPORTANT: Never close child tickets. The on-call engineer must make the rollback decision. Your role is to group, tag, and escalate child failures — not to update the root or resolve tickets.
